record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.original_question: Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for those chordal graphs that are circular-arc graphs. Here a circular-arc graph is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs on a circle, a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle on four or more vertices, and a forbidden induced subgraph characterization specifies which induced subgraphs must be absent exactly for membership in the class.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Give a forbidden induced subgraph characterization for circular-arc graphs within the class of chordal graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A circular-arc graph is the intersection graph of a family of open arcs on a circle: vertices correspond to arcs, with two vertices adjacent if and only if the corresponding arcs intersect. A graph is chordal if it contains no induced cycle on four or more vertices. A forbidden induced subgraph characterization of a graph class C is a (possibly infinite) family F of graphs such that a graph belongs to C if and only if it contains no member of F as an induced subgraph.

Problem: Determine an explicit forbidden induced subgraph characterization for the class of graphs that are simultaneously chordal and circular-arc graphs. That is, describe the complete list of minimal chordal graphs that are not circular-arc graphs.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of characterizing chordal circular-arc graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs remains open. Partial results exist: Bonomo–Grippo–Safe–Vatshelle (2013) characterized obstructions for chordal circular-arc graphs of small independence number; Francis–Hell–Stacho introduced the "blocking quadruple" obstruction; and Cao (2024) gave a complete forbidden induced subgraph characterization for the subclass of split graphs. A full characterization within all chordal graphs is not known.

status_evidence.title: Characterization of Circular-arc Graphs: I. Split Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The most elusive problem around the class of circular-arc graphs is identifying all minimal graphs that are not in this class. ... characterizes circular-arc graphs within the split graph subclass.
status_evidence.claim: The general forbidden induced subgraph problem remains unsolved; only the split-graph subcase is fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Obstructions to chordal circular-arc graphs of small independence number
status_evidence.snippet: Obstructions to chordal circular-arc graphs of small independence number.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results characterize obstructions only when independence number is small.

status_evidence.title: Blocking Quadruple: A New Obstruction to Circular-Arc Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The absence of blocking quadruples exactly characterizes chordal circular-arc graphs of independence number 4 or less.
status_evidence.claim: Blocking quadruples give a partial obstruction characterization within chordal graphs.
